posts.text: Saudi Arabia Reopens Riyadh Airport Even as Houthis Threaten Further Strikes — The Houthis, an Iran-backed Yemeni militia, launched several deadly attacks on the airport this month.

Gov. Wes Moore: 'People are pissed' over the Iran War — Maryland Governor Wes Moore says people are ‘pissed’ over the Iran War, as new reports emerge of a possible escalation of violence after the midterms. The war and the energy crisis have caused prices for almost all products to skyrocket, with the price of gas above four dollars a gallon nationwide.
How is the US-Israeli war on Iran causing havoc in Europe? — Rising energy costs and protests are sharpening European opposition to renewed US-Israeli attacks on Iran.
Saudi air defences intercept Houthi barrage near Mecca — Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalate as fierce ground battles and a devastating siege strangle Yemen's Taiz.

A New Level of Threat and Fear Risks Pushing the U.S. and Iran Back to Full War — With new intelligence and the possibility of all sides seeking pretexts for action, the war in Iran is entering a dangerous phase ahead of elections in the United States and Israel.
CENTCOM reportedly has plans for Iran strikes: Will Trump approve them? — Reports say Pentagon has drawn up plans for strikes after midterm polls, but analysts question what it could achieve.
Iran’s authorities take ‘self-sacrifice’ mobilisation campaign nationwide — The IRGC says it wants to use main squares in every capital of Iran’s 31 provinces for the Janfada campaign.

Former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot emerges as Netanyahu’s leading election challenger — A decorated former Israeli army chief has emerged as a leading election challenger after serving in the war cabinet and suffering devastating personal losses following the Oct. 7 attacks.
Iranians Face Anxious Wait as Threat of Attack Looms — The United States and Israel have drawn up plans to renew strikes against Iran, creating a sense of dread among war-weary residents.

Leavitt says Trump is defying midterm headwinds as he barnstorms country — Karoline Leavitt reveals Trump's blunt strategy to combat negative approval ratings and rally MAGA voters who typically skip midterm cycles.

Iran’s oil lifeline is drying up. The biggest pain may fall on ordinary citizens — Iran's floating oil inventory has fallen to zero as the U.S. naval blockade tightens, but the IRGC may be shielded while civilians bear the pain.

Soldiers guard center of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe — While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.

Obama compares Trump's White House renovations to 'Saddam Hussein opening a Cheesecake Factory' at Ohio rally — Barack Obama compared Trump's White House renovations to a Cheesecake Factory run by Saddam Hussein at a Cleveland rally for Ohio Democrats.

Iran in ‘Advanced Stages’ of Planning Attacks Against Americans, Officials Say — The U.S. government has ordered diplomats and other federal employees to leave Saudi Arabia. It is also drawing down staff at other missions in the region.

Nearly 1,000 arrested across France as police find potential weapons on protesters: officials — French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez says nearly 1,000 people were arrested as 70,000 police officers deployed across the country amid nationwide protests.

Attention, Passengers: High Airfares May Be Here to Stay — Ticket prices jumped after fuel costs spiked because of the war with Iran, but airlines say even an end to the conflict will not bring fares back down quickly.

U.S. is reducing staffing at 4 Middle East embassies over increased threats from Iran — In a memo sent Friday to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said his teams "have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel."
